edition.title: Kitāb Bughyat al-wuʿāh fī ṭabaqāt al-lughawiyyīn wa-l-nuḥāh
edition.editor: corrected by Muḥammad Amīn al-Khānjī with Aḥmad ibn al-Amīn al-Shinqīṭī

introduction: Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī (d. 911/1505) tells in his preface how the book came about. Grammar was the first of his sciences, and the lives of the grammarians he found were all short: al-Sīrāfī's Basrans, Abū al-Ṭayyib's Marātib, al-Zubaydī's Ṭabaqāt, al-Fīrūzābādī's Bulgha. In 868/1464 he set out to gather every grammarian and lexicographer he could find in the great histories, more than three hundred volumes of them, from al-Khaṭīb's history of Baghdad and Ibn ʿAsākir's of Damascus to the histories of al-Andalus, Egypt, Yemen and Mecca and the dictionaries of the ḥadīth scholars, until his draft filled seven volumes.

In Mecca a year later his friend the ḥāfiẓ Najm al-Dīn ibn Fahd advised him to draw from it one volume with the lives that matter, arranged as a dictionary. This is that volume, the Bughya: about 2,200 grammarians and lexicographers, from the first generations to al-Suyūṭī's own teachers, in the order of their names, those named Muḥammad first, then those named Aḥmad, then the other names letter by letter. Lists of kunyas, nicknames and nisbas follow, then names that several men share and names that are written alike, and the book ends with a chapter of ḥadīths that reached al-Suyūṭī through grammarians, taken from his larger ṭabaqāt.

The Bughya takes over much of what Ibn al-Anbārī, al-Zubaydī, al-Qifṭī and Yāqūt wrote, and adds the grammarians of the later centuries whom no earlier book had gathered. On this site it is the full reference beside Ibn al-Anbārī's Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ, which tells the story of the first centuries in order of death: each scholar's page links to his entries in both.

Our Arabic follows the first print, Cairo 1326/1908, corrected by Muḥammad Amīn al-Khānjī, who read it with al-Shaykh Aḥmad ibn al-Amīn al-Shinqīṭī, from a copy of the manuscript in the Khedivial Library. It is transcribed from the scan of that print and vocalised by us; the English is our own. The entries appear here as they are finished.
